name: checkpoints (P20)

R4.why: Own time, own kit, the stack's own integrity.

verdict.trigger: PROPOSAL_CHECKPOINTS §9 designed in full (crash handling, truncation, credentials, first checkpoints) and red-teamed again
verdict.change: The witnesses must be independent of the laptop, and an unreachable witness must not count as verified after 24 hours.

answers: Give the five gap fixes (ledger_v3, canon_verify_v3, store_v3, record_v3, substrate_v5) the one thing they cannot provide themselves: a trusted, current checkpoint, so rollback and substitution of the Legacy's own records become detectable.

answers.start: Supply trusted, current checkpoints to the gap fixes.
whys: Because each fix compares the data with a head or digest supplied from outside it, and nothing supplies one today.
Because a head read from the data itself, or an old checkpoint taken as current, cannot detect rollback (every draft SPEC says so).
Because nothing outside the data remembers what the latest state was; the ledger and store only prove their own internal chain.
Because the stack was built to prove who signed something and that it is intact, not that it is the newest version.
Because freshness needs a second, independent place that has seen the latest state: on one laptop, the data and its only memory can be rolled back together.

answers:
No key on the VPS.
No defence against a stolen owner key.
No automatic approval of substrate checkpoints.
No protection of history before the first checkpoint.

James can trust that the Legacy's ledger, store, records and substrate are the newest versions, and the Saboteur's rollback, substitution, deleted-row and unsigned-column threats can turn from red to healed.
By 2027-04-30, the rotation runs against the v3/v5 layers with checkpoints and at least 40 of the 154 known gaps show as healed, with 0 false rollback reports in 30 days of normal Legacy use.
James decides and signs. The Legacy writes checkpoints; the VPS witnesses them; the Saboteur proves them. Nobody outside James is waiting.
James owns it and signs the first checkpoints and every substrate approval.
Runs inside each Legacy write on the laptop; the witness push and comparison run on the VPS every 6 hours with the check. A failed push shows as unwitnessed in the daily report.
If it is wrong, a real rollback goes unnoticed, or a crash between writes is reported as an attack and James stops trusting the reports; records themselves are never changed by it.
James's time to sign the first checkpoints and substrate approvals, about 10 minutes a week. The witness file on the VPS is a few kilobytes.
Without it the five gap fixes cannot be switched on, so the 154 known gaps stay red; doing nothing leaves rollback and substitution of the Legacy's own records undetectable.
A signed git tag per change, a transparency log such as Sigstore Rekor, a timestamping authority, or doing nothing. Could reuse an open-source transparency log instead of the VPS witness.
No key on the VPS. Use the stack's own primitives (P2, P4, P16, P15). Frozen layers are never edited. Spare time only.
Checkpoints hold hashes, logical names and times only: no content, so they are safe on the VPS.
P2 sign, P4 ledger, P16 forge-time, P15 HAL, the VPS. All the stack's own; the VPS could be replaced by any second machine.
One checkpoint per write: a few hundred a month, each a few hundred bytes; at 10x still small.

1. P20 Checkpoint: a P4 ledger of signed checkpoints with the VPS as witness
2. A signed git tag per change, pushed to GitHub
3. Reuse an open-source transparency log (Sigstore Rekor)
4. Don't build it, park it: leave the fixes switched off

Option 1 is the stack's own primitives and needs one coordinated write. Git tags per write are heavy and public. A public transparency log is a third-party dependency with public entries. Parking keeps all 154 gaps red.

answers.chosen: P20 Checkpoint: a P4 ledger of signed checkpoints with the VPS as witness
answers.rejected: Git tags per change; a public transparency log; park it
answers.reason: It uses primitives the stack already trusts, keeps entries private to the stack, and the VPS already runs every 6 hours with no key.
answers.downside: One coordinated write in the Legacy, and freshness is unwitnessed while the laptop is offline.
answers.trigger: If more than 2 false rollback reports occur in 30 days of normal use, stop and redesign the coordinated write.

answers: The checkpoint log and the VPS witness, with prefix-plus-extension in ledger_v3 and store_v3, proven by the Saboteur on fixtures, by 2027-02-28.

A crash between the data write and the checkpoint write is rare and leaves a valid extension.
The VPS can keep a witness file and compare sequence numbers with no key.
James will sign substrate approvals within a week of each candidate.

The Saboteur kills the process between the data write and the checkpoint write on fixtures and checks the extension is accepted; a test against the VPS witness compares sequence numbers with no key present; the daily report shows how long each substrate candidate waits for James to sign.
The daily report lists each subject's checkpoint sequence, witness status (witnessed or unwitnessed) and any rollback or fork; a substrate candidate waiting for signature shows its age.
A crash between the data write and the checkpoint write is reported as a rollback, so James stops trusting the reports.

answers.start: A crash between writes is reported as a rollback.
whys: Because the verifier demands the data head equal the checkpoint exactly.
Because the drafts compare for equality and have no prefix-plus-extension mode.
Because the drafts were written before writes and checkpoints were coordinated.

answers: Someone with the owner key can forge checkpoints; someone who controls the VPS can refuse pushes, which shows as unwitnessed; replaying an old checkpoint is caught by the sequence number and the witness.
Add the prefix-plus-extension mode to the drafts so a crash between writes is accepted as a valid extension, and record each such crash in the daily report.
James approves every freeze and signs the first checkpoints and substrate approvals; the checkpoint ledger is the one source of truth; the CHANGELOG records each change.
The checkpoint ledger and the witness explain themselves to anyone with the public key; no handover capsule yet.
One command shows each subject's checkpoint, witness state and whether the data verifies against it.

answers.signal: By 2027-04-30 fewer than 40 known gaps are healed, or more than 2 false rollback reports occur in any 30 days
answers.then: James decides: redesign the coordinated write, or park P20 and leave the fixes off.

answers.reviewer: A fresh AI agent (Claude) that never saw the answers or how they were written; it checked claims against the stack's documents, read-only, 2026-11-23. Its facts were re-checked against the documents before use.
answers.found:
1. SECURITY & MISUSE / DECISION: the VPS witness is not independent of the laptop. The laptop already syncs whole databases there and holds the SSH and sudo path into it (roadmap/VPS.md rules 1 and 3), so whoever can roll back the laptop can usually rewrite the witness too. The witness would compare seq numbers without checking signatures, so a high-seq poison blocks every later verify. Re-checked: true.
2. OPERATIONS / SUCCESS: 'unwitnessed' counts as a pass, so roll back and then block the push. The run says the witness compares every 6 hours; the proposal says after every checkpoint. An unattended push after every write needs a new credential on the laptop (the current sync asks for a passphrase and sudo), which neither document designs.
3. RECOVERY / ROOT CAUSE: records and substrate stay exact-match, so a crash between a record write and its checkpoint still reads as rollback; prefix-plus-extension lets data written after the last checkpoint be truncated undetected; a torn half-line is not a valid signed extension.
Assumed as fact: 'primitives the stack already trusts' (ledger_v3, store_v3 and hal_v3 are drafts; re-checked true for hal_v3); Rekor rejected for public entries while the proposal calls checkpoints public data (re-checked: true); '10 minutes a week'; '40 of 154 healed'; 'a few hundred a month'; replay caught only while the witness is reachable and honest, and a fork at an equal seq is not covered; first checkpoints vouched for by frozen verifiers with a known rollback gap (0011).
answers.changing: Witnesses: three (VPS, S24, GitHub) instead of the VPS alone; each checks signatures and keeps only a higher seq; below any witness or a fork at equal seq FAILS; unwitnessed over 24 hours is STALE, not verified (PROPOSAL_CHECKPOINTS §9). Still to design: crash handling for records and substrate, truncation after the last checkpoint, torn lines, push credentials, cross-checking first checkpoints against the VPS's older copies.

evidence.fig: Each of the five draft SPECs requires an independently trusted, current checkpoint
